content:
Maria: Quick check — should SDKs expose retry/backoff per-call or via a client-level default for paginated endpoints? We're seeing divergent resume behavior between Python/TS/Go.
Jamal: Per-call gives users explicit control. Client defaults are fine but hard to override consistently.
Oliver: Per-call wins ergonomics-wise, but increases surface. Also we need clear idempotency guidance.
Erin: For read/list endpoints auto-retry is fine. For anything that can mutate state we should require explicit idempotency tokens or opt-out.
Maria: Proposal: default automatic retries only for safe "list/search" style APIs. Streams & resume tokens: return opaque token and do not auto-retry by default.
Jamal: Two implementation paths: 1) Add RetryOptions to call-level options across languages; 2) Annotate RPCs in the IDL with idempotency and let generators choose defaults.
Oliver: IDL annotations are cleaner long-term but slow to roll out. Short-term we should add call-level options to all SDK templates.
Erin: Also we should standardize a shared backoff table (initial, multiplier, max) in the SDK templates so Python/TS/Go behave the same out of the box.
Maria: Example TS ergonomics: 
```ts
client.listWidgets({pageSize:50}, {retry: {maxAttempts:3, baseDelayMs:200}})
```
Jamal: Python parity: 
```py
client.list_widgets(..., retry=Retry(max_attempts=3, base_delay=0.2))
```
Oliver: Important: resume tokens must be opaque. SDKs should not try to inspect/expand them for retry logic. If a retry is needed, the user re-sends with the token.
Erin: For streaming (HTTP/2 vs gRPC) keep the surface transport-agnostic: expose a resume token + checkpoint events on the client API, adapt internally per transport.
Maria: Operationally: add a linter that requires idempotency annotation for any endpoint that mutates state. That will force product teams to think through semantics.
sdk-bot: New issue created: INF-2345 - "SDK retry defaults and cursor semantics" (created by Maria) :white_check_mark:
Jamal: TL;DR agreement: 1) call-level RetryOptions across SDKs, 2) defaults only for safe reads, 3) opaque resume tokens + no automatic resume retries, 4) shared backoff table in templates. I'll draft a short RFC with migration plan. :thumbsup:
Erin: I'll add cross-language integration tests (mock server that injects transient failures and validates tokens/resume behavior).
Maria: Great — thanks everyone. Follow-up RFC from Jamal, tests from Erin, and I'll track the INF ticket.
